summary: Burst-window quota enforcement triggers stepwise 429s → streaming stalls for TheraSense; SDK retries amplify perceived timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer TheraSense reports intermittent streaming stalls during long-form generation. Sessions appear to hang for ~8–30s; client SDK then retries, which results in a sequence of 429s and eventual perceived timeouts. This ticket captures initial triage for a suspected burst-window quota enforcement interaction with the SDK's optimistic retries.

Impact:
- Affects a subset (~12%) of TheraSense production requests between 2026-03-13 14:10–15:40 UTC in us-east.
- Observed as partial or complete stream disconnects, increased tail latency, and elevated 429 rate for the customer's API key.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated; routed through dedicated pool id dp-33-us-east.
- Models: rw-llm-13b-v1 (primary), fallback to rw-chat-7b-v2.
- Client: thx-sdk-js v2.4.1 with default retry policy (3 retries, exponential backoff starting at 200ms).

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1. Open a streaming chat generation with a ~2000 token expected output.
2. Observe initial generation proceed for 2–6s, then connection stalls with no bytes for 8–30s.
3. SDK triggers a retry after client-side timeout; subsequent attempts get immediate 429 responses until the burst window resets.

Observed behavior:
- Service logs show a stepwise increase in 429 responses tied to per-customer burst-window token exhaustion on the rate-limiter.
- SDK retries cause a rapid succession of new connections which accelerate depletion of the customer's burst allowance, turning recoverable 429s into prolonged outages for the user.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming should either continue with graceful degradation (partial tokens) or throttling should be signaled in a way that clients back off (Retry-After) to prevent retry storms.

Relevant links/logs:
- Kibana trace samples: https://kibana.redwood.internal/app/discover#/SUP-20488-sample-traces (redacted link)
- Rate limiter dashboard (us-east/dp-33): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ratelimiter/dp-33
- Related status page event id: INC-20260313-therasense
comments: 2026-03-13 15:02 UTC - TheraSense (L. Moreno): We've had multiple customer sessions drop mid-stream. The page shows spinning and eventually the SDK retries and shows an error. This started after we pushed last night's model config; please advise.
2026-03-13 15:07 UTC - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Acknowledged — triaging. Can you share a request-id/sample timestamp when a session dropped? Also confirm SDK version and regional endpoint.
2026-03-13 15:12 UTC - TheraSense (L. Moreno): Sample request-id: req-20260313-8821; SDK v2.4.1; endpoint api.redwood.com (us-east).

2026-03-13 15:40 UTC - SRE (Marek Novak): Initial findings: burst-window counters for customer key show repeated drain events starting at 14:09 UTC. Logs indicate the client re-opened streaming connections ~4–10x within 30s after the first stall; each new connection consumed burst allowance immediately. Beginning deeper investigation into rate-limiter config and whether Retry-After headers were emitted.

2026-03-14 09:30 UTC - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Shared workaround with customer to temporarily increase client-side retry backoff and enable jitter (recommended: exponential backoff starting at 1s plus randomized jitter).
2026-03-14 12:10 UTC - TheraSense (L. Moreno): After applying the suggested backoff, incidents dropped to near-zero in the 3-hour window we tested. Thanks — please follow up with permanent change.
investigation_notes: Checked rate-limiter metrics for dp-33 pool: per-key burst tokens configured as 150 tokens with window 1m; sustained rate 5 qps. During incident, TheraSense saw spikes of short-lived concurrent streams equivalent to 40 qps for ~25s.
Examined serving-runtime logs for req-20260313-8821: initial stream produced ~1200 tokens, then a pause with no progress for ~12s; upstream kernel showed no GPU OOMs or preemption.

Confirmed that our API emitted 429s without a Retry-After header in several cases because the rate-limiter short-circuited at the proxy layer; SDK treats missing Retry-After as immediate eligible for retry per v2 behavior.

Client captures show SDK open→stall→close sequence; the SDK's retry loop opens a fresh stream which counts against burst allowance immediately (no smoothing), causing stepwise token-bucket exhaustion.

Hypothesis: combination of (a) burst-window conservative sizing for dedicated pool, (b) lack of Retry-After header on short-circuit 429s, and (c) aggressive client retry policy produced a retry amplification loop manifesting as perceived timeouts.
Ran a repro with internal test client mimicking SDK retry timing: observed identical pattern; inserting 800–1200ms randomized jitter prevented amplification and kept 429 rates within burst capacity.
Checked linked tickets SUP-155321 and SUP-84217 for similar retry amplification patterns — behavioral overlap but different root cause (those were soft-quota signals).
resolution: Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-14 09:40 UTC): Recommended customer to increase client retry base delay to 1s and enable jitter. Customer implemented and reported immediate reduction in incidents.

Immediate platform mitigation (2026-03-14 13:20 UTC): SRE adjusted dp-33 burst-window token allowance from 150→300 temporarily to reduce customer-facing failures during rollout. This is a stopgap while we implement header fix.

Root cause action items:
- Ensure rate-limiter returns Retry-After on short-circuit 429 responses where possible (ENG-kernerl, PR in progress).
- Evaluate and document per-customer burst-window sizing guidance for Dedicated pools; add an automated alert when sustained short spikes exceed 3x configured burst.
- Update SDK default retry policy in thx-sdk-js to treat missing Retry-After as soft-failure and apply conservative backoff with jitter (tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/thx-sdk-js/pull/312).

Follow-ups:
- Owner: Marek Novak to coordinate rate-limiter header fix (ETA 2026-03-20).
- Owner: Developer Experience to publish SDK guidance and ship updated default retry in v2.5.0 (ETA 2026-03-18).
- Customer follow-up scheduled 2026-03-18 to confirm behavior after fixes.
Status: Monitoring — platform mitigation applied; customer confirmed reduced failures in test window.
